findings.text: follow-on: the search in test_launch_callers_reach_the_shared_gate defines a launch path as a function that calls the names `_spawn` or `_start_supervisor` (lines 497-512), so §6 bullet 2's forward guarantee — 'a launch path added later without the gate read fails the test' — holds only for a path that reuses one of those two names. A launch path that starts a worker by another route is uncovered: appending a function that calls subprocess.Popen directly to reckon/crew/resumption.py leaves the test green (reproduced in /tmp/rev-gate-scratch, 1 passed), while appending a function that calls _spawn without the gate reddens it (reproduced, 1 failed). This is not hypothetical: the existing _supervisor_spawn_worker (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:10155) spawns the worker via subprocess.Popen and is not discovered by the search, so the supervisor's child spawn is gated only by its parent _start_supervisor's earlier read. Broadening the predicate to the spawn primitives (subprocess.Popen / _spawn_detached_worker / _spawn_detached_supervisor) or documenting the covered set in §6 would close the gap; the real launch decision is still gated, so this does not block landing.

justifications.durability: The guard is load-bearing and I falsified it. Removing the single _require_fleet_gate_open() call inside resumption._spawn reddens tests/test_the_fleet_gate_holds_dispatch.py::test_launch_callers_reach_the_shared_gate (reproduced at /tmp: 1 failed, EXIT=1), and the run's own negative-control.log records the same mutation red. The search also catches a newly added path that calls _spawn: appending a new function that calls _spawn without the gate reddens the same test (reproduced, 1 failed). It does NOT catch a newly added path that spawns the worker another way — appending a function that calls subprocess.Popen directly leaves the test green (reproduced, 1 passed) — and the existing _supervisor_spawn_worker (dispatch.py:10155) is exactly such an uncovered launch boundary, so the search's guarantee is narrower than §6 bullet 2 states. Recorded as the one finding.
justifications.evidence: The reviewed run records both the base and the head arm on disk. gate-head.log names revision 220eb563 and reports 202 passed, EXIT=0; after-suite.log (and gate-delivered.log) name revision 3f36e54bf and report 115 passed, EXIT=0; base-reproduction.log names 220eb563 and reports four of five launch callers lacking a direct fleet-gate read (UNGATED_CALLERS=4). I independently reran the search test at the head tree in a scratch extraction (/tmp/rev-gate-scratch, module /tmp/rev-gate-scratch/reckon/crew/resumption.py) and reproduced 1 passed, and reproduced the declared negative control (below) at EXIT=1. Weakness: the manifest's baseline_suite field is empty, so no same-command base arm is recorded; added-failure is derived from the base-revision arm the run does carry (gate-head.log) plus the head arm.
justifications.fit: The change extends the existing gate rather than adding a refusal family: a held launch is the existing LanePaused, raised by the new _require_fleet_gate_open() over the existing _dispatch_fleet_gate()/fleet_gate_path(); recovery.dispatch_repair_for_run catches LanePaused and records status lane-paused through the existing _record_repair_dispatch, and resumption._refusal_entry mirrors the BudgetHold branch to keep the prediction reading like the thing it predicts. The removed change_lane lane_gate-None fallback is dead given plan_dispatch always builds DispatchPlan(lane_gate=_dispatch_lane_gate(backend)) (dispatch.py:5932/5986), and the commit body names the removal.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §6 asks that every path that starts a worker be routed through the one fleet-gate read, dispatch/resume/redispatch/review+repair reflexes/recover/plan review. The diff adds _require_fleet_gate_open() (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4487) and calls it at the worker boundaries in dispatch._spawn (9399), dispatch._start_supervisor (10175), supervised_launch (10132), dispatch()'s two launch branches (8039/8043), cli.crew_resume (6866), resumption._spawn (751), resumption._resume (830), resumption._launcher_refusal (609) and mcp._crew_recover (4841), and change_lane reads resolution.lane_gate (12623); an AST search over reckon/*.py reports 5 launch callers, 0 ungated, and the named gate passes 115/115 at head 3f36e54bf (gate-delivered.log, EXIT=0). The one shortfall is that the search's coverage is name-keyed (below).
justifications.reuse: One helper is added, _require_fleet_gate_open(), and supervised_launch's and change_lane's duplicated inline fleet-gate reads are refactored onto it; the CLI/MCP/recovery surfaces reuse it rather than re-implementing the pause test. Nothing else is defined; the search test re-enumerates launch callers from the source with ast rather than a hand list, and reuses the existing lane_tests/repair_tests/review_plan_tests fixtures for the paused-vs-open controls.
justifications.scope_discipline: Both commits stay inside the declared write grants. 919a6d8ab and 3f36e54bf touch exactly reckon/cli.py, reckon/crew/dispatch.py, reckon/crew/resumption.py, reckon/crew/recovery.py, reckon/mcp.py, tests/test_dispatch_counts_worker_slots.py and tests/test_the_fleet_gate_holds_dispatch.py — all seven are recorded in the run pointer's write paths; no docs, plan, or index file is touched.
